request:
镜头 s38：纪录片细节特写镜头，时长 7 秒，16:9 横屏，24fps，单镜头一镜到底（只写 [Shot 1]）。
年代与画面风格（detailed_description 第一行照此英文书写）：raw verite documentary footage shot handheld in 2075 on a high-ISO full-frame documentary camera in available light only: visible sensor noise, deep solid blacks, volumetric haze and silhouettes, true-to-life skin tones, focus occasionally hunting
该类型的纪录片默认机位：documentary insert close-up grabbed handheld, focus breathing
导演意图（自然语言）：特写，固定。黑暗里，贴着笑脸贴纸的旧铁盒放在管道边上，小灯从红色变成绿色，连闪三下。环境声：三声轻轻的提示音。
情绪：hopeful, quiet, small
建议的景别与运镜（只做一个主要运镜）：close-up, locked-off
景深与虚实：The box and sticker sharp, the background black.
输入图片（按发送顺序；Subject N 对应 Picture N）：
Picture 1: the storyboard keyframe of this shot (opening frame). It shows: Insert in the dark: the old dented tin box with its antenna, now with the red-and-white ANET smiley sticker on its lid, sits on a pipe ledge; its small LED glows red. Blocking lock: the tin box sits at frame centre on a pipe ledge, the smiley sticker facing camera, darkness around.
Picture 2: the handmade ANET node box with the smiley sticker (prop reference; role: prop reference). Close-up product-less documentary photo of a handmade network node device on a workbench: an old dented steel ammunition tin fitted with a salvaged circuit board, a small heat sink, three tiny indicator LEDs (two red, one white) and a short screw-on antenna. On its lid is a slightly worn sticker that reproduces exactly the smiley speech-bubble logo from the reference image. Solder wire and a multimeter beside it.
本镜头没有台词。
现场环境声：three soft electronic chimes, distant hum
画面中没有字幕、文字、数字和水印；没有任何音乐和旁白；只说普通话。

attempts.output:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the dark pipe-ledge insert with the old dented tin box from <Picture 1>, serving as composition, lighting and blocking reference. A pitch-dark interior corner: a horizontal industrial pipe runs behind, and on a narrow metal ledge in front of it sits the handmade node box, lid toward camera. The only light is the box's own small indicator glow, a red point that rims the front edge of the tin and puts a faint red sheen on the pipe above; everything outside this small pool of light falls to solid black. The red-and-white smiley speech-bubble sticker is on the lid, facing camera, its edges slightly lifted and grimy. Palette: black, dull steel grey, one small red highlight. No text, numbers, captions or added marks anywhere in the frame; the sticker is an in-world object only. Blocking lock: the tin box at frame centre on the pipe ledge, the sticker face square to camera, the pipe a soft dark horizontal band behind it, empty blackness frame left, frame right and in the foreground.
<Subject 2> is the handmade ANET node box with the smiley sticker from <Picture 2>, serving as prop reference. An old dented steel ammunition tin, dark olive-grey, paint chipped to bare metal along the corners and the lid seam, shallow dents on the lid and one long scratch across the front; the lid carries a short screw-on antenna, slightly bent, and a salvaged circuit board with a small heat sink is fitted at its side, with three tiny indicator LEDs (two red, one white) set in a rough drilled row and loose solder joints visible around them. On the lid, a slightly worn sticker reproducing the red-and-white smiley speech-bubble logo, its paper yellowed at the edges, one corner curled, surface scuffed but the smiley still legible as a picture. Must read as real practical wear: metal reflections, fine scratches, oxidised dark spots and dust in the seams, not a new craft piece. Prohibited: readable words, letters, numbers, serials or printed labels of any kind on the tin or the sticker; no added text.

summary:
In near-total darkness an insert close-up holds on the old dented tin node box, its smiley sticker facing camera, resting on a pipe ledge in a 2075 shelter interior. Its small indicator light shifts from red to green and blinks three times, each blink answered by a soft electronic chime. The clip ends on the green light steady again, the box and sticker sharp at frame centre, the background pure black.

retention_analysis:

<Subject 2> (appears in this shot): fully_preserved — shape, dents, chipped paint, antenna, circuit board, LEDs and the worn smiley sticker retained as the prop.

detailed_description:
16:9 horizontal, single clip 7.0s, 24fps, raw verite documentary footage shot handheld in 2075 on a high-ISO full-frame documentary camera in available light only: visible sensor noise, deep solid blacks, volumetric haze and silhouettes, true-to-life skin tones, focus occasionally hunting; real documentary footage, not a movie, not CGI, unposed; no hard subtitles, no burned-in captions, no on-screen text, no logo, watermark or platform bugs.
[Shot 1] At 0.0s, close-up, locked-off camera braced on a small support, framing held unchanged from close-up to close-up for the whole take, no move; pacing: natural speed, a single continuous take with no cut. The tin box sits at frame centre on the pipe ledge, sticker face square to camera; the pipe is a soft dark horizontal band behind it; frame left, frame right and the foreground are empty black. Start: the box rests motionless, the small indicator LED a steady red point that breathes faintly against the steel, dust drifting in the thin haze above the lid. Middle: the red fades, the LED comes up green, and it blinks three times in an even slow rhythm, each pulse briefly lighting the curled corner of the sticker and the chipped rim of the tin, the focus easing a touch and settling back on the sticker face. End: the third blink closes and the green light stays on, steady and small, the antenna casting a thin shadow on the pipe behind; the frame holds on the box unchanged. Mood: hopeful, quiet, small. Blur: the box and the smiley sticker sharp, the pipe softening at its far edges, the background falling away into pure black. No character speaks any line in this shot; any human voices are indistinct, unintelligible Mandarin Chinese walla only. Hold the last frame.

overall_soundscape:
Three soft electronic chimes spaced evenly through the take, a low continuous hum of distant machinery, faint ticking from the warming metal of the pipe, a whisper of air moving in the duct behind the box; raw production location sound only, dry and unscored, no background music.
